title: The Asymmetric Effect of Reporting Flexibility on Priced Risk

scopes.description: The complete author-supplied Stata preparation and analysis workflow that builds the risk-asymmetry inputs and runs its OLS, SOX 404/RDD, placebo, reconvergence, and internal-control analyses.

requirements.description: CRSP daily stock observations imported as CRSP_daily_FULL.dta. The code uses PERMCO, SICCD, RET and DATE to merge daily factors and construct excess returns, then firm-specific weekly returns/crash-risk measures. The local legacy DSF core is readable, and its separate name-history table has effective-dated SICCD; source join/cardinality and the full daily construction history remain unverified.

routes.description: CRSP.DSF is locally readable for the bounded core fields. The author input also needs SICCD; the separately probed CRSP.DSENAMES table has PERMNO, PERMCO, NAMEDT, NAMEENDT, SICCD and EXCHCD. Their date-effective join, author-export contract and full history/cardinality remain unverified.

requirements.description: Fama-French daily factor panel read as FFFactors.dta and merged by DATE to CRSP daily returns; the author needs RF and MKTRF. This is a joint but separate input from CRSP returns.

routes.description: The local Fama-French daily factor product exposes the author-required date, market and risk-free fields in a one-row read. Convert to the Stata input format and validate the exact required period/vintage.

requirements.description: CRSP monthly stock observations imported as CRSP_monthly_FULL.dta. The code uses PERMCO, DATE, RET, PRC, SHROUT, VOL, BID, ASK and EXCHCD to build fiscal-year mappings and annual size/age/volume/spread/volatility characteristics. Local MSF core fields are readable; EXCHCD/SICCD require a separate date-effective name-history candidate, with full period and cardinality unresolved.

routes.description: CRSP.MSF is locally readable for the bounded author core fields. The code also requires EXCHCD (and daily SICCD); separately probed CRSP.MSENAMES supplies EXCHCD/SICCD with PERMNO and effective dates. Conversion, date-effective join/cardinality and full history remain unverified.

requirements.description: Author-prepared CRSP/Compustat merged annual panel read as CRSP:CompustatMergedFundamentalsAnnual.dta. It supplies firm-year, fiscal-year-end, GVKEY/LPERMCO/CIK, SIC/SICH and accounting inputs for mapping, EDR, characteristics, SOX/internal-control samples and analysis. Local COMP.FUNDA core fields and a separate historical link-table candidate are readable, but their mapping does not establish the author's full panel, special fields/definitions or construction-period contract.

routes.location: WRDS CRSP/Compustat Merged Annual Fundamentals; author filename CRSP:CompustatMergedFundamentalsAnnual.dta
routes.description: This is the named author-prepared merged annual panel described by the datasheet. The exact prepared export is not in the archive and its field/history contract has not been verified; current entitlement is not assessed.

COMP.FUNDA is a locally readable raw annual-fundamentals candidate for constructing a Stata panel. A separate CRSP.CCMXPF_LINKTABLE probe exposes GVKEY/LPERMCO/link dates, but the candidate pair is not a verified replacement for the author panel and does not settle CIK, SIC/SICH, SOX/internal-control fields/definitions, historical links or full-period coverage.

requirements.description: SIC-to-Fama-French-48 lookup CSV read as SICtoFF48.csv with ffnum, ffcode, ffdesc, startsic and endsic. It is used for FF48 assignment in EDR and characteristics and is absent from the package; the current official public SIC definitions are a candidate pending schema/vintage matching.

routes.description: Official Ken French 48-industry SIC definitions are a public candidate. The official page confirms SIC-based industry assignment, but the author's required ffnum/ffcode/ffdesc/startsic/endsic CSV schema and historical vintage must be matched before conversion.

requirements.description: The separate Compustat Non-Historical Segments product read as Segments.dta supplies GVKEY, DATADATE and SID to derive a log segment control. A local merged-segments product has those fields in a bounded read; full period and source/vintage compatibility remain unverified.

routes.description: The local merged-segments candidate exposes the fields read by the author routine. Verify the non-historical segments product/vintage, full period and Stata conversion.

requirements.description: Iliev public-float input read as public-float-data-complete.csv uses publicfloat, fiscalyear, publicfloatyear, gvkey and cik to form 2002/2004 values and merge by GVKEY. issues.description: Legacy CRSP.DSF/MSF and their name-history tables expose plausible fields for the author panels, including SICCD and monthly EXCHCD with PERMNO and effective dates. The author DTA source join, effective-date boundary, cardinality, PERMCO consistency, time coverage and source-vintage contract are not verified by one-row reads.

The exact author-prepared merged annual panel includes LPERMCO, GVKEY/CIK, fiscal-year/SIC and accounting fields plus SOX/internal-control definitions. COMP.FUNDA and the historical link table are readable candidates, but they do not verify the author's merged panel, special source fields or their definitions. Preserve those gaps rather than guessing a link or formula.

The public Ken French SIC definitions support a candidate source, but the author-required five-column CSV and its historical mapping vintage have not been matched. The official SIC classification page does not establish exact author row values.

The public farr iliev_2010 dataset is an Iliev-source candidate but already stores publicfloat in $ million and uses FYEAR/PFYEAR names; the author code expects dollar values divided by 1,000,000 and fiscalyear/publicfloatyear. The public release also documents date corrections, so values/vintage need explicit comparison before substitution.

Stata 18, reghdfe 6.12.3, ftools 2.49.1 and the actual _gxtile implementation used by egen xtile() are available in the checked environment. The supplied program also invokes winsor2 and runby; neither was found by the bounded checks in the default/separately checked shared adopaths, so those commands need local preparation before a future run.

The 2020 historical log contains a separate output macro and outreg2 XLS table exports that are not in the supplied .do/PDF mirror. The supplied .do remains the assessed program; clarify the intended source variant only if those historical table files are required as an output.

evidence.quote:
Attached to this Data Description Sheet, please find: (1) a .do file for use in Stata; (2) a
  .pdf version of the .do file; and (3) a Stata log file, documenting the data processing, and
  key regression results. Note that the observation counts reported in the log-file regressions
  do not necessarily match the observation counts reported in the paper. This discrepancy
  is attributable to REGHDF E, which reports the number of observations after dropping
  singletons. In contrast, I report the sample size inclusive of singletons. The final samples
  used in the main analyses can be found in the excel files FullSample PERMCOs.csv and
  RDDSample PERMCOs.csv, both using PERMCO firm identifiers.
  The .do file can be run in Stata for Mac simply by acquiring the necessary raw data (de-
  scribed in item 1 of this Data Description Sheet), placing the raw data in a working directory,
  and changing the local variable ‘data’ to match the working directory (line 2).
  NOTE: Stata packages change over time which can cause slight differences in results. For
  example, the REGHDF E package (used for all of the regressions) is regularly updated, and
  occasionally these updates can have material impacts such as: (1) changes to the syntax
  of a REGHDF E call; (2) changes to the calculations of clustered standard errors. Slight
  differences are to be expected, depending on vintage.
evidence.description: The author says the archive contains a Stata .do, PDF mirror and historical log, names the two PERMCO CSVs as final-sample identifiers, and describes the required raw-data working-directory setup and reghdfe singleton-count distinction.

evidence.quote:
**Earnings downside risk
use "`data'/CRSP:CompustatMergedFundamentalsAnnual.dta", clear
keep if fyear>=1982
gen firm=lpermco
drop if missing(firm, fyear, revt)
sort firm fyear revt
by firm fyear: drop if fyear==fyear[_n+1]
sort firm fyear
by firm: gen avgat=(at+at[_n-1])/2
gen roa=ib/avgat
gen sales=sale/at
gen size=log(prcc_f*csho)
gen lev=(dltt+dlc)/at
sort firm fyear
by firm: gen roa_3=roa[_n-2]
by firm: gen roa_4=roa[_n-3]
by firm: gen roa_5=roa[_n-4]
gen roa_mean=(roa_3+roa_4+roa_5)/3
gen std_roa=sqrt(((roa_3-roa_mean)^2+(roa_4-roa_mean)^2+(roa_5-roa_mean)^2)/2)
gen oc=log(360*(rect/sale+invt/cogs))
winsor2 roa sales size lev std_roa oc, replace cuts(1,99)
sort firm fyear
by firm: gen roa_lead=roa[_n+1]
save "`data'/edrtemp.dta", replace
evidence.description: Annual fundamentals supply inputs to EDR construction, including lagged and lead ROA variables.

evidence.quote:
insheet using "`data'/SICtoFF48.csv", clear
keep ffnum ffcode ffdesc startsic endsic
cross using "`data'/sich.dta"
keep if inrange(sich, startsic, endsic)
merge 1:m sich using "`data'/edrtemp.dta", nogenerate keep(match)
save "`data'/edrtemp.dta", replace
expand(3)
keep firm fyear roa_lead roa sales size lev std_roa oc fyear ffnum
order firm fyear roa_lead roa sales size lev std_roa oc fyear ffnum
sort firm fyear
sort firm fyear
by firm fyear: gen regyear=fyear+_n-1
sort firm regyear
statsby, by(ffnum regyear) nodots clear: regress roa_lead roa sales size lev std_roa oc
rename regyear fyear
merge 1:m ffnum fyear using "`data'/edrtemp.dta", keep(match) nogenerate
gen resid=roa-(_b_cons + _b_roa*roa + _b_sales*sales + _b_size*size + _b_lev*lev + _b_std_roa*roa +_b_oc*oc)
save "`data'/edrtemp.dta", replace
use "`data'/edrtemp.dta", clear
sort firm fyear
by firm: gen lower=sqrt(1/3*((resid*(resid<0))^2+(resid[_n-1]*(resid[_n-1]<0))^2+(resid[_n-2]*(resid[_n-2]<0))^2))
by firm: gen upper=sqrt(1/3*((resid*(resid>=0))^2+(resid[_n-1]*(resid[_n-1]>=0))^2+(resid[_n-2]*(resid[_n-2]>=0))^2))
replace lower=sqrt(1/2*((resid*(resid<0))^2+(resid[_n-1]*(resid[_n-1]<0))^2)) if lower==.
replace upper=sqrt(1/2*((resid*(resid>=0))^2+(resid[_n-1]*(resid[_n-1]>=0))^2)) if upper==.
gen edr=log((1+lower)/(1+upper))
keep firm fyear edr
replace edr=0 if edr==.
save "`data'/edr.dta", replace
evidence.description: The EDR workflow uses SICtoFF48.csv and a forward ROA lead; its firm-year residual measure uses 3-year/2-year rolling residual windows.

review_notes: Scope: the complete supplied Reporting Flexibility code.do preparation and analysis workflow. The two included PERMCO CSVs are identifier lists, not usable author-prepared analysis panels.

Local SAS resources were checked only with bounded one-row reads. A readable sample is not evidence of full-period coverage or nonmissing values; missing values in individual sampled rows are not field or population absence.

Legacy CRSP DSF/MSF plus DSENAMES/MSENAMES provide a conditional field-mapping candidate. Effective-date joins, cardinality, source-vintage equivalence and history remain unverified; the current DSF_V2/MSF_V2 products are not automatic replacements.

The local COMP.FUNDA and CCMXPF link-table probes are candidates only. They do not establish the author's merged annual panel, its CIK/SIC/SOX/internal-control fields, definitions or link construction.

Public Ken French SIC definitions and the current CRAN farr Iliev table are source candidates. The author SIC CSV schema/vintage and Iliev public-float units, field names and corrected dates must be reconciled before use.
Stata 18, reghdfe 6.12.3 and ftools 2.49.1 are available in the checked environment. winsor2 and runby were not found in the checked paths and need local preparation; no install was attempted.

The code's EDR history uses ROA leads/lags and current-plus-two-prior residual windows. The estimation source specifies firm/year-by-fiscal-year/industry absorbed effects and ffnum/fyear clustering; it contains no IV estimator or instrument construction.

The historical 2020 log is evidence of that earlier run only. Its 130 firm-specific-return by-group errors are not a current execution finding. The datasheet itself explains the paper/log singleton-count difference.
The historical log's output macro and outreg2 exports are absent from the supplied .do/PDF source pair. outreg2 is not included as a current .do software dependency.
